guarantees.claim: process_valid is cleared to 0 on reset (rst_ni low)
process_valid is set to 1 when start_i is asserted, taking priority over process_i
process_valid is cleared to 0 when process_i is asserted and start_i is low
process_valid holds its previous value when neither start_i nor process_i is asserted and no reset

assumptions.claim: The consumer of process_valid must eventually assert process_i to deassert process_valid after a start event.
assumptions.risk: If process_i is never asserted, process_valid remains high indefinitely, potentially causing downstream deadlock or incorrect padding termination.

uncertain_points.claim: If start_i and process_i are asserted simultaneously, the priority logic keeps process_valid at 1; confirm whether this restart/extension behavior is intended or could cause an overrun.
uncertain_points.risk: Unintended extension of the processing window may allow extra data or corrupt padding if downstream logic expects a strict handshake.
